title: What Happens To Your Body When You Drink Coffee

lines.text: If you drink a cup of coffee,
lines.caps: If you drink | a cup of | coffee,

lines.text: the caffeine starts slipping from your gut into your blood within minutes.
lines.caps: the caffeine starts | slipping from your | gut into your | blood within minutes.

lines.text: It races up to your brain,
lines.caps: It races up | to your brain,

lines.text: where a chemical called adenosine has been building up all day, making you sleepy.
lines.caps: where a chemical | called adenosine has | been building up | all day, | making you sleepy.

lines.text: But caffeine looks so similar that it steals adenosine's parking spots,
lines.caps: But caffeine looks | so similar that | it steals adenosine's | parking spots,

lines.text: so your brain never gets the message that it's tired.

lines.text: your heart beats a little faster,
lines.caps: your heart beats | a little faster,

lines.text: and the blood vessels in your head tighten.

lines.text: It even wakes up your gut, which is why coffee can send you to the bathroom.

lines.text: And with a half life of about five hours,

lines.text: an afternoon coffee is still half in your blood at bedtime.
